senses.en: the feeling of wanting sth. that sb. else has
examples: They only say such unkind things about you out of [[envy]].

senses.en: wish that you had sb. else's possessions, abilities, etc.
examples: I [[envy]] her ability to talk confidently to people she has never met before.

senses.en: give sb. great satisfaction and enjoyment
examples: Her recipe will [[delight]] anyone who loves chocolate.

senses.en: very pleased and happy
examples: Thanks for your invitation. I'd be [[delighted]] to come.

senses.zh: 把（某人）列入入围（决选）名单
senses.en: (usu. passive) (BrE) put sb. on a short list for a job or a prize
examples: He was [[shortlisted]] for the Nobel Prize for Literature several times.

senses.zh: （因震惊、惊恐等而）感到心猛地一跳，胃里猛地翻腾了一下
senses.en: if your heart or stomach lurches, it seems to move suddenly because you feel shocked, frightened, etc.
examples: Virginia's heart [[lurched]] painfully in her chest on hearing the news.

senses.zh: 突然不稳地行走（移动）；蹒跚而行
senses.en: walk or move suddenly in an uncontrolled or unsteady way
examples: Suddenly the horse [[lurched]] to one side and the child fell off.

senses.zh: （因震惊、兴奋或醉酒）头晕，感到天旋地转
senses.en: (spun, spun) if your head or the room is spinning you feel as if you might faint because you are shocked, excited, or drunk
examples: I was pouring with sweat, and my head was [[spinning]].

senses.en: (spun, spun) (cause to) turn round and round fast
examples: He [[spun]] the wheel sharply and made a U turn in the middle of the road.

senses.zh: （尤指因生气或不安）握紧，绷紧，咬紧
senses.en: if you clench a part of your body such as your hand or your mouth, or if it clenches, you close it tightly, esp. because you are angry or upset
examples: Through [[clenched]] teeth she told him to leave.

senses.zh: （使）（身体的某一部分）变得僵硬，变得僵直
senses.en: become stiff or make a part of your body become stiff
examples: Sofia's throat had [[tightened]] and she couldn't speak.

senses.en: close or fasten sth. firmly by turning it
examples: I'd put the new tyre on and [[tightened]] up the wheel.

senses.zh: （将计算机屏幕上的信息）上下滚动，滚屏（以便阅读）
senses.en: move information on a computer screen up or down so that you can read it
examples: [[Scroll]] to the end of the document and you will find what you need.

senses.en: slightly
examples: He was [[vaguely]] aware of footsteps behind him.

senses.en: chance or luck, and the effect that it has on your life
examples: I had the good [[fortune]] to work with a brilliant head of department.

senses.en: a very large amount of money
examples: He made his [[fortune]] in car sales.

senses.zh: 激发，激起（强烈的感情）；引起（强烈的反应）
senses.en: make sb. have a strong feeling or reaction
examples: Looking at the photographs [[stirred]] childhood memories of the long hot summers.

senses.en: move a liquid or substance around with a spoon or stick in order to mix it together
examples: [[Stir]] the paint to make sure it is smooth.

senses.en: (not before noun) specially protected from sth. unpleasant
examples: The criminal was told that he would be [[immune]] from prosecution (起诉) if he helped the police.

senses.en: safe from a disease, because you cannot be infected by it
examples: This blood test will show whether or not you're [[immune]] to the disease.

senses.zh: 令人不安的；使人烦恼的
senses.en: worrying or upsetting
examples: There was something about him that she found very [[disturbing]].

senses.en: relating to the way that your mind works and the way that this affects your behavior
examples: Robyn's loss of memory is a [[psychological]] problem, rather than a physical one.

senses.en: (only before noun) relating to treating or testing people who are sick
examples: The therapy has helped people with [[clinical]] depression.

senses.zh: （因顾虑自己的外表或他人的看法）忸怩的，害羞的，不自然的
senses.en: worried and embarrassed about what you look like or what other people think of you
examples: Bess was [[self-conscious]] about being shorter than her two friends.

senses.en: websites and software programs used for social networking
examples: [[Social media]] is changing the way people communicate, work, and shop.

senses.en: a good idea about what you should do, write, say, etc., esp. one which you get suddenly
examples: Dreams are a rich source of [[inspiration]] for some writers.

senses.en: the application of cosmetics
examples: I got my wedding [[makeup]] done in this beauty studio.

senses.en: causing damage to people or things
examples: Lack of trust is very [[destructive]] in a relationship.

senses.en: wanting sth. that sb. else has
examples: I'm so [[envious]] of you getting an extra day's holiday.

senses.en: sb. who is trained to treat people with a mental illness by talking to them instead of giving them drugs
feel angry or upset about a situation or about sth. that sb. has done, esp. because you think that it is not fair
examples: I [[resented]] having to work such long hours.

senses.zh: （对不公平的事）愤恨的，不满的，憎恶的
senses.en: feeling angry and upset about sth. that you think is unfair
examples: They were bitterly [[resentful]] of the fact that they had to work such long hours.

senses.en: a feeling of being comfortable, healthy, and happy
examples: The warm sunny weather always gives me a sense of [[well-being]].

senses.zh: 强烈的欲望；迫切的要求；冲动
senses.en: a strong wish or need
examples: He could no longer resist the [[urge]] to go and see Amanda.

senses.zh: 竭力主张；强烈要求；敦促
senses.en: strongly suggest that sb. do sth.
examples: They [[urged]] Parliament to approve plans for their reform program.

senses.en: able to be easily harmed or hurt
examples: Their constant arguments left her feeling increasingly [[vulnerable]] and insecure.

senses.en: the feeling of being satisfied with your own abilities, and that you deserve to be liked or respected
examples: Educated people are found to have higher [[self-esteem]].

senses.en: the lack of sth. that you need in order to be healthy, comfortable, or happy
examples: Sleep [[deprivation]] can result in mental disorders.

senses.en: willingness to allow people to do, say, or believe what they want without criticizing or punishing them
examples: He shows little [[tolerance]] for people with different views.

senses.en: unwillingness to accept ways of thinking and behaving that are different from your own
examples: The party was accused of stirring up a climate of fear and [[intolerance]].

senses.zh: 值得尊敬的；值得注意的；值得敬仰的
senses.en: deserving respect, attention, or admiration
examples: The money we raise will be going to a very [[worthy]] cause.

senses.en: recognize or express the difference between things or people
examples: It's important to [[differentiate]] between fact and opinion.

senses.en: not normal or natural and likely to be harmful
examples: Frank has developed what I would term an [[unhealthy]] relationship with these people.

senses.zh: 对健康有害的；会致病的
senses.en: likely to make you ill
examples: He worked in the [[unhealthy]] environment of a coal mine.

senses.en: the feeling that you need to eat
examples: I can't believe that that enormous meal wasn't enough to satisfy your [[hunger]].

senses.en: lack of food, esp. for a long period of time, that can cause illness or death
examples: Is it possible to end poverty and [[hunger]] in a decade?

senses.en: (~ with) happen at the same time as sth. else, esp. by chance
examples: I timed my holiday to [[coincide]] with the children's school holiday.

senses.zh: 不安全；没有自信；没有把握
senses.en: the state of not feeling at all confident about yourself, your abilities, or your relationships with people
examples: She had developed an outgoing personality to mask her deep [[insecurities]].

senses.en: working independently for different companies rather than being employed by one particular company
examples: He has been a [[freelance]] journalist for the BBC for a decade.
Now I am chief of pediatric [[neurosurgery]] at John Hopkins Children's Center in Baltimore.

senses.zh: 惊人的；骇人的；令人难以置信的
senses.en: very surprising, upsetting, and difficult to believe
examples: It is [[shocking]] that they involved children in the crime.

senses.en: encourage or help an activity to begin or develop further
examples: The government should do more to [[stimulate]] investment in the rural areas of the state.

senses.en: officially tell sb. what to do
examples: He [[instructed]] his men to collect information about troop movements.

senses.en: two things that are unrelated are not connected to each other in any way
examples: The police think that the two incidents are [[unrelated]].

senses.en: having or showing good health and strength
examples: He looks [[robust]] and healthy.

senses.zh: （感觉、态度、行动）富于感染力的，会蔓延的
senses.en: if a feeling, attitude, or action is contagious, other people are quickly affected by it and begin to have it or do it
examples: Daffy has a [[contagious]] enthusiasm for life and poetry.

senses.en: a disease that is contagious can be passed from person to person by touch
examples: Mumps (腮腺炎) can be a [[contagious]] disease.

senses.en: when people laugh, or the sound of people laughing
examples: He delivered the line perfectly, and everybody roared with [[laughter]].

senses.zh: 引起，促使，导致（尤指精神或身体的变化）
senses.en: (fml.) cause sth., esp. a mental or physical change
examples: Taking a brisk walk can often [[induce]] a feeling of well-being.

senses.zh: 劝诱，诱导（尤指做似乎不明智的事）
senses.en: (fml.) persuade sb. to do sth., esp. sth. that does not seem wise
examples: Nothing would [[induce]] me to take that job.

senses.en: the length of time that sth. continues
examples: For the [[duration]] of the strike our shop will remain closed.

senses.en: the quality of being felt very strongly or having a strong effect
examples: The storm started again with even greater [[intensity]].

senses.en: a feeling or an impression caused by a particular experience
examples: I can remember the first time I went sailing — it was a wonderful [[sensation]].

senses.en: a feeling that you get from one of your five senses, esp. the sense of touch
examples: Massage (按摩) produces wonderful [[sensations]].

senses.en: needing electricity to work, produced by electricity, or used for carrying electricity
examples: The [[electric]] guitar, along with rock-and-roll, rose to popularity around the world.

senses.en: (~ sb. / sth. with sth.) make a connection in your mind between one person or thing and another
examples: Most people [[associate]] this brand with good quality.

senses.en: sb. with whom you work or do business with
examples: They have been business [[associates]] for decades.

senses.en: sth. that is not directly said or shown, but that is suggested or understood
examples: I resent the [[implication]] that my work is not thorough.

senses.zh: （行动、事件、决定等的）可能的影响（后果）
senses.en: a possible future effect or result of an action, event, decision, etc.
examples: The new report has far-reaching [[implications]] for the future of broadcasting.

senses.en: surprise sb. very much
examples: What [[astonished]] me most was her lack of common sense.

senses.en: so surprising that it is difficult to believe
examples: It's [[astonishing]] how much the place has changed.

senses.en: (also 'neurone')
connected with electricity; using or producing electricity
examples: Since the Great Depression, every new [[electrical]] appliance has come with a promise that it would transform the home.

senses.en: (only before noun) relating to music or consisting of music
examples: She has no formal [[musical]] qualifications.

senses.en: (BrE favourable) suitable and likely to make sth. happen or succeed
examples: The disease spreads quickly under [[favorable]] conditions.

senses.en: (BrE favourable) a favorable report, opinion, or reaction shows that you think sb. / sth. is good or that you agree with them
examples: We have had a [[favorable]] response to the plan so far.

senses.zh: 加强，强化（观点、思想、感觉等）
senses.en: give support to an opinion, idea, feeling, etc. and make it stronger and more likely to continue
examples: The latest figures [[reinforce]] the view that economic growth is slowing down.

senses.en: a strong feeling of uncontrollable anger
examples: He would sometimes fly into a [[rage]] for no reason at all.

senses.en: an imaginary or ancient creature that is large, ugly, and frightening
examples: A terrifying [[monster]] attacked the helpless villagers.

senses.en: (infml.) near and easy to reach
examples: Keep your pills [[handy]] just in case you feel seasick.

senses.en: useful
examples: It's very [[handy]] having a light above your desk.

senses.en: (~ to / with) if two or more facts, ideas, etc. correlate or if you correlate them, they are closely connected to each other or one causes the other
examples: Stress levels [[correlate]] strongly with heart disease.

senses.zh: （人或动物的）寿命，预期生命期限
senses.en: the length of time that a person or animal lives or is expected to live
examples: Worms have a [[lifespan]] of a few months.

senses.en: used when you are mentioning a fact that you wish was not true
examples: [[Unfortunately]], you were out when we called.

senses.en: showing no emotion, understanding, or interest
examples: Zoe looked at me with a [[blank]] expression.

senses.en: without any writing, print, or recorded sound
examples: Sign your name in the [[blank]] space at the bottom of the form.

senses.en: into or inside a building
examples: Mother was advised to stay [[indoors]] for a week after her cough seemed better.

senses.en: kept in prison or in a place that you are not allowed to leave
examples: She was kidnapped and held [[captive]] for over a week.

senses.en: sb. who is kept as a prisoner
examples: They freed their [[captives]] before surrendering.

senses.zh: 可能发生的事；可能出现的情况
senses.en: a situation that could possibly happen
examples: Imagine a [[scenario]] where only 20 percent of people have a job.

senses.en: when a person or animal is kept in a prison, cage, etc. and not allowed to go where they want
examples: Animals bred in [[captivity]] would probably not survive if they were released into the wild.

senses.en: (also 'automatic pilot') a machine that flies a plane by itself without the need for a pilot

senses.zh: 凡是你说得出的（应有尽有）
senses.en: (spoken) used after a list of things to mean that there are many more you could mention
examples: Vodka, whisky, beer — [[you name it]], I've got it.

senses.en: not have the chance to do sth. that you enjoy or that would be good for you
examples: Well, I'm glad you could make it; I didn't want you to [[miss out]].

senses.en: concerning
examples: One of the biggest things that should happen [[in relation to]] the Internet is that kids and adults, too, should be taught to manage it.

senses.en: be good enough to do a particular job or to reach a particular standard
examples: How will the Secretary General [[measure up]] to his new responsibilities?

senses.en: (infml.) when the subject being discussed is a particular thing
examples: He's a bit of an expert [[when it comes to]] computers.

senses.en: (also 'every so often') sometimes, but not often or regularly
examples: He cleans out his desk drawers [[every now and then]].

senses.en: try very hard to improve or achieve sth.
examples: We need to [[work on]] ensuring that the children feel safe and confident.

senses.zh: （信息、事实等逐渐）被充分理解
senses.en: if information, facts, etc. sink in, you gradually understand them or realize their full meaning
examples: He paused a moment for his words to [[sink in]].

senses.en: used to say that what you are saying about one thing is also true about sth. else
examples: Ben never touched beer, or any kind of alcohol [[for that matter]].

senses.en: as a way of being safe from sth. that might happen or might be true
examples: Take an umbrella, [[in case]] it rains.

senses.en: based on a calculation about how many times sth. usually happens, how much money sb. usually gets, how often people usually do sth., etc.
examples: My income's rather variable, but I earn £73 a day [[on average]].

senses.zh: 正在做（秘密或不该做的事）
senses.en: (spoken) doing sth. secret or sth. that you should not be doing
examples: The children are very quiet. I wonder what they're [[up to]].

senses.en: the opposite of what you have just mentioned
examples: Now the reality was just [[the other way round]].

senses.zh: 亚里士多德（古希腊哲学家、科学家）
雷切尔 · 安德鲁（人名）
帕特里夏 · 波莱德里（人名）
伊扎克 · 弗里德（人名）
